title: fix(fleet): give the claim refusal an amendment arm for a card already dispatched
body:

_Requested by **Irene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x?thread=cmsg_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x8Be2AAcUBhodBsvnWLd3Xs)_
Refs #36454 (item 2)
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感:只改车队内部写评论的工具;修改认领评论被拒时,提示里多出一条适合「已派发卡」的写法。
- 属于车队巡检与签章工具的维护,替所有修改已派发卡认领的席位解决「提示给错写法」的问题。
- 出错时只是提示文字不对,工具本身不写任何东西;可以直接撤回这次改动。
- 无

## What changes

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` refuses a comment that opens `Claim:` (on every route but `direct`) and used to print one stroke, `label-write.mjs --issue N --comment-file PATH --add pm:dispatched --remove pm:queue --assign LOGIN`, whatever the card's state. On a claim amendment the card is already `pm:dispatched` and assigned, and that stroke adds LOGIN as a second assignee unless LOGIN already holds the card.

The refusal now prints two arms, each under the card state it fits:

- a card not yet dispatched (`pm:queue`): the stroke above, unchanged;
- a card already `pm:dispatched` (a claim amendment): `label-write.mjs --issue N --comment-file PATH --add pm:dispatched`.

The refusal stays pure (the suggested route's option b): the body cannot tell a first claim from an amendment, and a card-state read that fails must not print a confident wrong stroke. Printing both arms is safe because label-write refuses a wrong pick of the amendment arm on a card that carries another pm state (two state labels, ONE-OF, nothing written). A card with no pm state at all is not refused: there the amendment arm would dispatch it with no assignee, so the refusal names the first arm for it, "a card not yet dispatched (`pm:queue` or no pm state)" (L1 patch round 1, record 7139217309). Kept as they were: the fold is relay-only, a route resolved `direct` still posts the claim here, and the refusal is still outside `judgeBody`. The docblock, the JSDoc and `--help` say the second arm.

Line budget: 49 changed lines (+41 / -8) in one file, inside the ~150 budget.

## Tests

`node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs --self-test` at `63a45590`: `✓ post-stamped self-test: 813 cases pass across 30 batteries` (807 before; the claim-stroke battery pin goes from 15 to 21). At `58100e07` it read 812; patch round 1 added the no-pm-state control (both arms through label-write on a card labelled `domain:skills` only: the amendment arm packs `comment > labels_add` with no `assign`, the dispatch arm packs `comment > labels_add > assign`); its ablation (dropping ` or no pm state` from the first-arm label) read `✗ 1 of 813 case(s) failed`. New cases:

- both arms print, each under its state line; the amendment arm is the dispatch arm minus `--remove pm:queue --assign LOGIN`;
- the amendment arm taken from the printed text, run as label-write's own dry run (child process, fake card read, no network) on a dispatched and assigned card: exit 0, one stroke whose only op is `comment`;
- control one step away: the same arm on a card still `pm:queue`: exit 2, ONE-OF, no stroke packed;
- control: the dispatch arm on that dispatched card, LOGIN another account, packs `comment > assign` (the second assignee);
- the dispatch arm on a `pm:queue` card still packs `comment > labels_add > labels_remove > assign`.

Two one-off ablations, each mutation committed first, applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 to 0) and restored byte-identical to the HEAD blob:

<details><summary>Ablation readings</summary>

- delete the amendment-arm line from `claimStrokeRefusalText`: `✗ post-stamped self-test: 3 of 812 case(s) failed` (two-arm text, amendment arm through label-write, the queue control). Restore blob `5a16ec8b` = HEAD blob.
- in `label-write.mjs` (not in this diff), make `planned` ignore `--add`: `✗ post-stamped self-test: 2 of 812 case(s) failed` (both amendment-arm label-write cases). This shows the cross-tool pin goes red if label-write stops taking a no-op `--add` beside `--comment-file`. Restore blob `514254c3` = HEAD blob.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Measured before choosing the stroke (dispatch assumption 2): label-write's `planned` check reads the flags, not their effect, and `computeLabelTarget` treats an add of a label already on the card as an idempotent no-op. So `--add pm:dispatched --comment-file F` on a dispatched card packs one relay stroke whose only action is the comment. The old stroke worked mechanically only when LOGIN was already the assignee; with any other login it packed `comment > assign`.
- Dispatch assumption 3: the protocol has no separate amendment shape. An amendment is a newer `Claim:` comment with the same keyed lines, and the patrol reads the newest one (`latestClaimComment` and the claim-state reader in `check-half-states.mjs`). The amendment arm leaves labels and assignee as they were, so the board the patrol reads afterwards is the one it read before, with the newer claim governing.
- Not in this PR: card item 1 (the patrol token's `checks: read`). Its premise was not measured, and the seat holds it.
- Changeset: none, `skip-changeset`. `scripts/pm/**` is fleet tooling that no package ships.

## Verification

Read first, by risk:

1. `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs`, `claimStrokeRefusalText`: the two arms and the sentence about why each fits its state.
2. The same file, the claim-stroke battery: the `lw(...)` probe that runs each printed arm through label-write's dry run.

Two-minute check: `node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs --self-test`. Expected: `✓ post-stamped self-test: 813 cases pass across 30 batteries`, and six new cases under `the claim stroke`.
